Dear Appeal Coordinator,

I am writing to formally appeal Aetna Better Health of West Virginia’s denial of the prior authorization request for my lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT code 63030), which was recommended and submitted by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Duval. 

The denial letter dated August 19, 2026, states that “the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.” This determination is medically incorrect and directly contradicted by my clinical records. I have extensively tried and failed conservative therapy, far exceeding the requirements set forth in your plan’s governing medical policy. 

### I. Applicable Medical Policy and Criteria
According to Aetna’s Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) **0743**, titled **“Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion”**, a lumbar laminectomy/discectomy is considered medically necessary when the following criteria are met:

1.  **“All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out...”**
2.  **“Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated”**
3.  **“Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings”**
4.  **“Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 *...”**
5.  **“Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression”**

Furthermore, the policy's **“Footnote1*”** explicitly defines the conservative therapy expectation as follows:
> **“Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression.”**

### II. Demonstration of Compliance with Medical Policy

My medical records clearly demonstrate that I meet every single criterion outlined in CPB 0743, including an exhaustive and documented conservative treatment trial:

1.  **Failed Conservative Therapy (Exceeds Policy Requirements):** 
    *   **In-Person Physical Therapy:** I completed a **12-week trial of supervised, in-person physical therapy** from April 13, 2026, to July 06, 2026, at [Physical Therapy Facility Name]. This program included core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. I attended and completed **16 visits**, as fully documented in my attached physical therapy discharge note. This 12-week program is double the 6-week duration required by your policy.
    *   **Conservative Medications:** I have been taking prescribed NSAIDs for **8 months** with completely inadequate relief of my symptoms. 
    *   **Interventional Care:** On May 25, 2026, I underwent a corticosteroid injection [at Clinic/Facility Name]. This invasive conservative measure yielded only 4 weeks of partial relief before my severe symptoms returned, further demonstrating the failure of non-surgical management.
2.  **Advanced Imaging Indicating Compression/Stenosis:** My lumbar spine MRI dated June 23, 2026, shows an **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root**. This satisfies the requirement for advanced imaging indicating "severe" stenosis and "nerve root" compression.
3.  **Clinical Signs and Symptoms of Neural Compression:** I have suffered from progressive lower back pain for **18 months**, which is completely unrelieved by rest. Dr. Duval’s clinical examination revealed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a corresponding objective neurological deficit that maps precisely to my L5 nerve root and the L4-L5 disc extrusion imaged on my MRI. I experience severe radicular pain radiating down into my right calf.
4.  **Functional Limitation (ADLs):** My symptoms of neural compression have severely limited my activities of daily living. Due to the intense radicular pain and structural compression, I am **unable to stand for more than 10 minutes** at a time.
5.  **Rule Out of Other Sources:** All other reasonable sources of pain and neurological deficit have been ruled out by Dr. Duval. I am a non-smoker, have a BMI of 29, have no active infections, and have no untreated substance use.

### III. Conclusion

The clinical evidence attached to this appeal proves that my conservative treatment trial was not only adequate but was double the length of Aetna's policy standard. Because my 12 weeks of active, in-person physical therapy and 8 months of NSAIDs have failed to resolve my severe nerve compression and functional impairment, surgical decompression under CPT 63030 is the only medically necessary and appropriate next step.

I request that you immediately overturn this denial and approve the requested lower back disc surgery. Please find attached my physical therapy discharge records, my June 23, 2026 MRI report, and Dr. Duval's clinical notes.

If you require any further information, please contact my provider, Dr. Duval, or me immediately.

Sincerely,

Morgan Lawson
